learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the fascinating world of biotechnology, its historical evolution, and how it merges biology with technology to improve human life!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: The European Federation of Biotechnology (EFB) defines it as the integration of natural science and organisms, cells, or parts thereof, for products and services. It's using biology to invent useful things.

Traditional biotech includes making curd, bread, and wine using natural microbes. Modern biotech involves manipulating DNA (Genetic Engineering) to create genetically modified organisms (GMOs) like Bt Cotton or synthetic insulin.
The technique of altering the chemistry of genetic material (DNA and RNA) and introducing it into host organisms to change their phenotype.
Maintaining sterile (microbe-free) environments in chemical engineering processes to allow only the desired microbe/cell to grow in large quantities for manufacturing vaccines, enzymes, etc.
Biotechnology has revolutionized healthcare (gene therapy, vaccines), agriculture (pest-resistant crops), and the environment (bioremediation/cleaning up pollution).

fun_activity.title: 🍞 The Kitchen Scientist
fun_activity.instructions: You are a traditional biotechnologist! Take some warm milk, add a spoonful of old curd (starter), and leave it overnight. The Lactobacillus bacteria will ferment the milk into curd. You just performed a biotech process!

exam_tips: 📌 Always write the exact definition of Biotechnology as given by the European Federation of Biotechnology (EFB).
📌 Distinguish clearly between Genetic Engineering (changing the DNA) and Bioprocess Engineering (growing the cells in a sterile environment).
📌 Remember that the discovery of restriction enzymes (molecular scissors) and plasmids paved the way for modern genetic engineering.
quick_recap: ⭐ Biotechnology is as old as human civilization (making bread/cheese), but modern biotech is driven by DNA manipulation.
⭐ The core principles of modern biotech are genetic engineering and bioprocess engineering.
⭐ GMOs (Genetically Modified Organisms) are created by inserting foreign DNA into a host.
